headline: ENERGY FUELS $1.9B DEAL CREATES FIRST US MINE-TO-MAGNET RARE EARTH COMPANY — VAC'S 400 PATENTS AND SC FACILITY SCALABLE TO 12,000 TPA NdFeB
source_name: PR Newswire / Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: UUUU) announced June 23 a definitive agreement to acquire Vacuumschmelze GmbH & Co. KG (VAC) from Ara Partners for approximately $1.9 billion in total consideration ($718M cash + 65.85 million new UUUU shares), creating the first fully vertically integrated US rare earth company spanning uranium-backed mine operations, rare earth oxide separation, and downstream NdFeB permanent magnet manufacturing at VAC's Sumter, South Carolina facility — capacity scalable from 2,000 to 12,000 tonnes per annum. VAC, founded over a century ago, holds 400+ patents and has shipped over one billion permanent magnets to more than 1,000 customers across EV, wind, aerospace, and defense sectors; combined with Energy Fuels' White Mesa mill operations and its January 2026 acquisition of Australian Strategic Materials, the deal gives UUUU the only fully western mine-to-magnet rare earth supply chain outside Chinese control at the moment China has simultaneously blacklisted US rare earth producers MP Materials and USA Rare Earth — a strategic compression that makes the VAC acquisition one of the most consequential rare earth supply chain moves of the decade.

headline: GOLD FALLS TO $4,129 — 2-MONTH LOW AS DEUTSCHE BANK AND BOFA BOTH ADD SEPTEMBER RATE HIKE TO FED FORECASTS
snippet: Gold fell to $4,129 per ounce on June 23, 2026 — its lowest close in approximately two months and roughly 26% below the January all-time high of $5,589 — as both Deutsche Bank and BofA Global Research added explicit September rate hike projections to their Federal Reserve forecasts, joining Goldman Sachs' $4,900 year-end target revision from June 21; simultaneously, the US-Iran 60-day oil export licence announced late last week has eased the geopolitical risk premium that had partially supported gold since the conflict began February 28. The week's pivotal data are Friday's Core PCE inflation reading (the Fed's preferred benchmark) and Monday's June flash PMI releases: a soft PCE print relative to consensus would immediately reprice the probability of a Warsh rate hike before December, and historically has been the single most reliable trigger for a sharp gold recovery after a correction driven by Fed hawkishness rather than a structural change in the bull market thesis.

headline: LITHIUM HITS 10-WEEK LOW: CATL JIANXIAWO MINE RESTART SPECULATION WIPES 10% IN TWO SESSIONS
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices in China dropped to CNY 157,000 per tonne — their lowest in ten weeks — as speculation intensified that Contemporary Amperex Technology's Jianxiawo mine in Jiangxi province, suspended last year due to permitting issues, may restart in the second half of 2026 following a government land assessment notice interpreted by traders as a procedural milestone for re-approval. The Jianxiawo mine accounts for an estimated 3% of global lithium production, and while analysts note that the government notice does not confirm a reopening timeline and that supply-demand conditions are expected to remain relatively tight as significant new battery manufacturing capacity comes online in Q3 2026, the prospect of any supply addition in a market that has already recovered 162% year-over-year at CNY 157,000/t is sufficient to trigger institutional de-risking ahead of confirmation. For retail investors tracking TSXV and ASX lithium developers, the episode illustrates the binary risk that single-mine news events still impose on lithium prices at current volume levels, and reinforces the thesis that western-hemisphere projects with offtake agreements are structurally de-risked relative to pure-play exposure to Chinese spot prices.

headline: COPPER SECTION 232 D-DAY JUNE 30 — COMMERCE SECRETARY REPORT DETERMINES 15% TARIFF IN 2027, 30% IN 2028 ON REFINED COPPER
snippet: The US Secretary of Commerce must deliver a domestic copper market assessment to President Trump by June 30, 2026, with the findings determining whether to implement the next phase of the Section 232 copper framework: a phased universal import duty of 15% on refined copper effective January 1, 2027, rising to 30% from January 1, 2028 — on top of the 50% tariffs already imposed on semi-finished copper products since August 2025. For junior copper miners and advanced developers on the TSX-V and ASX, confirmation of the refined copper tariff schedule would be the most structurally bullish single policy event of 2026: it would permanently advantage North American producers selling domestically — who face no export tariff — relative to imported refined copper from Chile, Peru, and Asia, accelerating the valuation re-rating of Canadian and American copper development projects that began after the semi-finished product tariffs were confirmed. The June 30 deadline is this week; market participants are watching for any Commerce Department statements signalling the recommendation's direction.

headline: SILVER BOW MINING BUTTE: FIRST HOLES EXTEND RAINBOW BLOCK CRITICAL MINERALS ZONE UP TO 2,270 FEET BEYOND RESOURCE
source_name: Yahoo Finance / Silver Bow Mining Corp. (NYSE American: SBMT)
snippet: Silver Bow Mining Corp. (NYSE American: SBMT) reported June 22 that the first two holes of its 25,000-foot surface diamond drilling program at the Rainbow Block Project in Butte, Montana have extended critical mineral mineralization substantially beyond the current inferred resource boundary: hole SBM26-01 intersected silver-zinc-indium-lead-gold mineralization from 640 to 1,980 feet beyond the resource along strike, and SBM26-02 confirmed the critical minerals package from 930 to 2,270 feet beyond the boundary — both holes drilled above the water table to minimise development cost. Every metal identified in the program — silver, zinc, indium, lead, and gold — holds a US government Critical Mineral designation, positioning the Butte Rainbow Block as one of the few primary silver projects in the continental United States with a multi-critical-mineral co-product profile that could qualify for domestic supply chain incentives and strategic materials purchasing from US government offtakers, a market channel not available to conventional silver-only projects.

headline: SPROTT: CAMECO CEO WARNS "WALL OF UNCOVERED URANIUM DEMAND" THROUGH 2045 — UTILITY CONTRACTING GAP "NEVER BIGGER" IN 30 YEARS
snippet: Sprott Asset Management's latest uranium market analysis underscores Cameco Corporation's president and COO, who stated that the volume of uncovered uranium requirements — future utility demand not yet secured under long-term supply contracts — has reached record levels and that 'between now and 2045, that is a wall of demand that ultimately cannot be avoided.' With uranium spot prices holding at $85-86 per pound and Cameco reporting Q1 2026 net income up 87% year-over-year alongside a separately announced $2.6 billion long-term supply agreement with India covering approximately 22 million pounds of uranium concentrate through 2035, the structural thesis for uranium rests on a contracting cycle that has only just begun: utilities spent 2022-2024 deliberately under-contracting as a cost management strategy that is now reversing as the 78-plus gigawatts of nuclear capacity currently under construction globally requires fuel supply commitments that have not yet been placed — a forward demand backlog with no viable non-uranium alternative.

headline: JIM ROGERS: "I'M BUYING SILVER, NOT GOLD RIGHT NOW" — LEGENDARY INVESTOR CITES 63:1 RATIO AND SOLAR DEMAND FLOOR
snippet: Legendary investor Jim Rogers — co-founder of the Quantum Fund alongside George Soros and creator of the Rogers International Commodities Index — told GoldSeek that he is actively buying silver in preference to gold at current prices, citing the gold-to-silver ratio near 63:1 as historically elevated relative to what industrial demand from solar panels, EV batteries, and electronics manufacturing has made a permanent structural demand floor that gold does not share. Rogers observes that the Silver Institute's projection of a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces in 2026 combined with a 63:1 ratio above the long-run equilibrium range of 50–55:1 is the combination that has historically preceded silver's largest multi-month outperformance relative to gold — a view consistent with silver's 9.4% gain in June 2026 to date against gold's 0.4% advance, which is silver's second-best June performance in modern history.

headline: SILVER PRICE OUTLOOK JUNE 2026: THE CORRECTION WAS THE SETUP — SIXTH DEFICIT YEAR UNCHANGED AS SOLAR DEMAND HITS RECORD
snippet: GoldSilver.com's June 2026 silver price analysis argues that silver's 45% correction from its January 2026 record of $121.64 per ounce to the current $66-67 range has not impaired the structural bull market thesis: the Silver Institute projects a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces in 2026, solar panel manufacturing is consuming silver at a record pace that makes photovoltaic applications the largest single source of new silver demand for the first time in modern market history, and the gold-to-silver ratio near 63:1 is the same elevated reading that preceded every major silver outperformance cycle of the last 25 years — most recently 2016 and 2020, when silver's outperformance of gold over the following 12 months ranged from 35 to 120 percentage points. The piece identifies the current setup as structurally distinct from the 2012–2014 silver bear market because the industrial demand floor from electrification is not present in prior corrections, making each dollar of price decline a greater compression of the mine supply incentive price rather than a correction toward fundamental value.

headline: GOLDSEEK GOLD SWOT: ASIAN ETFs KEEP ADDING GOLD EVEN AS US AND EUROPEAN FUNDS BLEED — EAST-WEST DIVERGENCE WIDENS
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT analysis for June 23, 2026 identifies an accelerating divergence between Asian and Western gold ETF flows as the most significant structural development of the current correction cycle: Asian gold-backed ETFs — led by China-domiciled funds and Indian gold ETFs — have continued to build bullion holdings even as US-domiciled GLD and IAU, and major European gold ETFs, have seen sustained net outflows since gold's January all-time high of $5,589 per ounce. The analysis notes that Sprott estimates central bank net purchases are on pace for 650-plus tonnes in 2026, and that the combination of Asian institutional accumulation and central bank demand provides a structural demand floor beneath the current price that did not exist during the 2012–2014 gold bear market — meaning the current correction has fundamental demand support that the prior cycle lacked, and that Western speculative liquidation is creating the entry window rather than signalling a structural bear market.

headline: THE GOLD TREND THAT MAY SURPRISE 2026: MINERS FINALLY OUTPERFORM THE METAL AS RECORD MARGINS FORCE A RE-RATING
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's current analysis argues that the most market-moving gold story of 2026 will not be the price recovery — which most forecasters already embed — but gold mining equities finally outperforming the gold price itself after years of structural underperformance: with GDXJ delivering a 203% price return in the twelve months to February 2026, senior producers posting record quarterly cash flows (Coeur Mining $267M free cash flow in Q1 2026, Hecla Mining $144M), and the sector averaging approximately 16.9x trailing earnings while generating 137% year-over-year operating cash flow growth, the historical valuation discount of gold miners relative to the metal is compressing for the first time since the 2015-2016 cycle bottom. The piece identifies the June 2026 correction low as the last clean entry point before the market recognises that miners producing gold at $4,100–$4,200 with all-in sustaining costs below $1,800 per ounce are generating free cash flow yields that would be re-rated violently in any other sector — and that the window where retail investors can still buy miners at a discount to intrinsic value is closing.
